cases.question: Who owns invoice export, and why is it still on the old runner?
cases.golden_answer: Data Platform owns invoice-export [owns-invoice]. It is observed on legacy-runner [run-invoice-legacy]; its migration ticket depends on open network approval, owned by Security [tracks-invoice-migration, blocked-network, status-network-open, owns-network]. Decision temporary-exception permits continued use until 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z [permits-invoice]. This is permission, not proof that continued use is mandatory. Billing requires invoice export [requires-billing-invoice]. Retirement is blocked; reporting coverage also remains stale.

cases.question: What breaks for billing if the network approval slips a week?
cases.golden_answer: Assume the one-week slip moves the proposed decision point from 17 to 24 October 2026. Based on evidence known on 17 October, network approval still blocks invoice migration [blocked-network, status-network-open]. Retiring legacy-runner while this dependency remains would affect invoice export and therefore monthly billing [run-invoice-legacy, requires-billing-invoice]. The slip alone does not prove a billing outage or missed invoice deadline: there is no billing execution calendar or future verification in these records. Continued use is permitted through 1 November by temporary-exception [permits-invoice], so 24 October is inside that permission interval; this does not authorize retirement. Security owns approval [owns-network]. Reverify usage and reporting coverage before acting; do not predict that future work completes.
